title: Are Chinese Superbikes Finally This Good? (X-Lab AD9 Review)

takeaways.text: He cites US$8,000 for the AD9 as tested, with Dura-Ace Di2, X-LAB carbon cranks with a dual-sided power meter and carbon-spoked wheels, below comparable Western flagships.
His size L test bike weighed 6.8 kg without pedals on his scales.
The distinctive fork dropout tabs looked thin enough that he worried about damage in a bike bag; he found no aero claim for them.
Finish details he would improve: only one supplied aero cage, which does not sit flush, and a team livery applied as a sticker with a palpable edge.
Over several months it showed no creaks, loosening bolts or seatpost slip, and the bottom bracket is a threaded T47.
He found it fast and stiff but firm over rough roads; the carbon-spoked wheels added to that, and a steel-spoked wheelset gave a slightly smoother ride.
At 180 cm on a size L he wanted a longer stem; with a one-piece cockpit and no UK dealer at the time, he could not easily swap it.
The 165 mm cranks took him time to adapt to, mainly in saddle height and the feel of torque.

disclosure: The creator describes the bike as a demo bike that goes back after testing; the description links the brand site and the channel's sponsors, a clothing brand and a camera maker.
summary: An August 2026 review of a size L X-LAB AD9 demo bike after several months, built with Shimano Dura-Ace Di2, X-LAB power-meter cranks and carbon-spoked wheels. That test build differs from the mainland Vision-wheel build recorded here.
